title: Derived global internal Hom detects shifted maps from a fixed native module object
statement: Let X be a scheme and Λ a commutative condensed coefficient ring. Use native internal modules over its pulled-back coefficient ring and their unbounded derived category [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Let K,N,N′ be objects and f:N→N′. Write RHom for the existing native derived internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] and RΓ_ab for the functor obtained by forgetting the coefficient action termwise and then deriving abelian-sheaf global sections [def-sfb-finite-model-topology-comparison-maps]. If RΓ_ab(RHom(K,f)) is an isomorphism, then for every integer n the function Hom(K,N[n])→Hom(K,N′[n]), g↦g followed by f[n], is bijective. No boundedness, constructibility, flatness or nonzero-ring hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: The ordinary free-module functor R tensor - preserves quasi-isomorphisms between K-flat complexes. An acyclic K-flat complex remains acyclic under tensoring with R (CochainComplex.acyclic_tensorRight_of_kFlat); braid the tensor factors and use the faithful exact module forgetful functor to reflect acyclicity. Package this in the source PreservesKFlatQuasiIso criterion. Derive free/forgetful and constant-sheaf/global-sections adjunctions using Adjunction.derivedAdjunction, and use the exact-functor comparison on forgetting and constant sheaves. Their composite right adjoint is exactly the specified sections functor.

proof.text: The derived composite left adjoint sends the integer group in degree zero to the native derived monoidal unit. Constant sheaf is strong monoidal. The single complex on its unit is K-flat; the derived free counit is therefore invertible there. Compose its K-flat counit with the single/derived-quotient and single/map-complex comparisons, the explicit free-unit isomorphism (the ordinary right unitor), and DerivedCategory.singleFunctorObjUnitIso. All objects and isomorphisms are actual constructions.

proof.text: For an arbitrary integer n, shift the integer test object by -n. The composite left adjoint commutes with shifts, by the mate of the right adjoint shift structure. Tensoring K with its image gives K[-n], using the source derived tensor shift structure and the right unitor. Compose the shift adjunction, this tensor-unit isomorphism, and the composite adjunction with K tensor - left adjoint to native RHom(K,-). This yields natural bijections Hom(K,Y[n]) with Hom(Z[-n], sections(RHom(K,Y))).

source.place: Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U, global statement; Tags 0A95 and 0A96; the natural global Hom complex calculation, including all integer shifts.

proof.text: Adjunction naturality identifies postcomposition by f[n] with postcomposition by sections(RHom(K,f)). The latter is bijective since the assumed arrow is an isomorphism. Transport its injectivity and surjectivity through the preceding equivalences. This covers negative shifts, zero rings and the empty scheme without extra hypotheses.

theorem shiftedHom_bijective_of_globalInternalHom_isIso
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{u}) Ab.{u + 1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (K : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ X)))
    {N N' : DerivedCategory (Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (condensedRingObj Λ X))} (f : N ⟶ N')
    (h : IsIso ((sections X (condensedRingObj Λ X)).map
      (((CondensedRing.derivedHom Λ X).obj (op K)).map f))) (n : ℤ) :
    Function.Bijective (fun g : K ⟶ N⟦n⟧ ↦ g ≫ f⟦n⟧')
